approach: Fix the stop rule where it starts: `Drain::finish` in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, arm `ItemEnd::Failed` (line 2379), which sets `Stop::RepeatedFailure` for any one item. Add a `failures: Vec<(String item, String key)>` field to `State` (built at ~line 2305). In `finish`, one lock section reads the item's last `JobLine`, derives a normalized cause key, looks for an earlier DIFFERENT item with the same non-empty key, and records this item's key. If one matches, the cause is shared, so `set_stop(Stop::RepeatedFailure, Some(item.job))` and a note names the earlier item. Otherwise `pass_over(item.job, "failed twice, paused for this run: <reason>")` plus a note, and the worker takes the next item exactly as for `ItemEnd::Paused` and `ItemEnd::Skipped`. The cause key is the landing text after `not landed: ` when the last line has one, else the run reason. It is lower-cased and split on whitespace; a token equal to the item's name or its retry job's name, or shaped like a job id, becomes `<job>`; and it is re-joined with single spaces. An empty reason has no key (unknown cause), so it is never counted as shared. Matching is whole-token, never substring, because item names such as `a` would otherwise corrupt the text. Environment stops (rebuild failure, reinstall, disk hold, budget, job limit) are untouched. Then update the doc comments, display text, `--help` text, README, a decision record, the CHANGELOG and the old-rule tests, and add the new tests.

decisions.choice: Judge a shared cause by a normalized failure reason compared across two different items, kept in `State`.
decisions.reason: The brief's accepted reading says so. The reason already sits on the item's last `JobLine`: `reason` for a rejected/failed run, `landing` for a landing failure. It needs no new record or Steps method, so the fix is one focused change in `finish`. Check-and-insert happens under the state lock, so two concurrent workers cannot both miss each other.

rejected.option: Stop on any two failed items regardless of reason.
rejected.why: Two unrelated item failures would end the batch, which is the fault in a milder form. Criterion 3 requires different reasons to continue.

rejected.option: Classify the cause by outcome kind only (rejected / failed / not landed).
rejected.why: Too coarse: two rejections for unrelated verifier findings would look shared. The reason text carries more.

rejected.option: Add a Steps method that asks the environment whether it is healthy.
rejected.why: Widens the trait and every stub and impl for a rule that the existing line data can answer. Environment failures already have their own stops.

decisions.choice: An empty failure reason has no key and is never treated as shared.
decisions.reason: With no stated cause, calling two failures shared would be a guess that stops the batch. Pausing the item is the safe default. The Shared test stub returns an empty reason for rejections today, so the producer gives its failing items a reason in the tests that need a shared stop.

rejected.option: Key on outcome plus reason, so empty-reason rejections match.
rejected.why: It would stop the batch for any two silent rejections.

decisions.choice: Match whole whitespace-delimited tokens when stripping item and job names; do not replace substrings.
decisions.reason: Test items are named `a` and `b`. A substring replace turns 'checks failed' into 'checks f<job>iled' for item `a` and leaves it intact for `b`, so equal causes would look different.

rejected.why: Breaks on short names, as above.
Possibly not a dependency of this crate; token logic is enough. This was not checked.

decisions.choice: Keep `Report::failed_item` for the shared-cause stop only (the later item); name the earlier item in a note. The display line keeps the prefix `repeated failure: item X failed twice` and adds the shared-cause wording.
decisions.reason: No new Report field means the JSON shape and the existing display assertions stay valid. Notes already print as `note` lines.

rejected.why: Changes the serialized report for a detail a note carries.

decisions.choice: The failed item stays in `report.queued` and is not retried in this run.
decisions.reason: `State.tried` already keeps a handed-out item from being offered again, and `pass_over` logs once per item per run via `passed_over`. This matches Paused and Skipped.

rejected.option: Persist a pause record for the item.
rejected.why: Out of scope (the scope guard and its pauses are untouched) and would add a record kind.

decisions.choice: Do not touch athena.toml, defaults.toml, ATTEMPTS or the reader's skip rule.
decisions.reason: The brief lists them out of scope. `failures >= ATTEMPTS` in `attempts` stays as is; only what `ItemEnd::Failed` does changes.

steps: Read `Drain::finish`, `State` and its construction (~line 2305), and `Drain::push` / `JobLine` in drain.rs. Confirm that the item's last `JobLine` carries both the run `reason` and the `landing` text.
In drain.rs add `failures: Vec<(String, String)>` to `State` (item, key) and initialise it empty where `State` is built.

Add a pure fn `failure_key(reason: &str, names: &[&str]) -> Option<String>`: lower-case, split on whitespace, trim edge punctuation, map a token that equals a name or looks like a job id (`dddddddd-dddddd-xxxx`) to `<job>`, rejoin with single spaces, and return None when the result is empty. Add `Drain::cause_of(&self, item, last_job) -> Option<String>`: take the item's last JobLine, use `landing` minus the `not landed: ` prefix when it starts with that, else `reason`, and call `failure_key` with the names [item.job, line.job].

Change `finish`'s `ItemEnd::Failed` arm. Under one `self.st()` lock compute the key, find an entry for a different item with an equal Some(key), and push (item, key). If it matched, `set_stop(Stop::RepeatedFailure, Some(item.job))` and `note("item {item} failed twice for the same cause as item {earlier}: {reason}; the run stops")`. Otherwise `note("item {item} failed twice and is paused for this run: {reason}")` and `pass_over(&item.job, "failed twice, paused: {reason}")`. Never call a Steps method with the lock held (the file's own rule, lines 1096-1097). `finish` has no `last_job`, so either add it to the arm via `ItemEnd::Failed` or read the last line's own job name; the item's last JobLine already has it.

risks.risk: The real run reasons (`f.reason` from athena_core::run::Finished, drain.rs line 3545) may embed text that differs per item (job ids, paths, counts), so a true shared cause is missed and the batch pauses items one by one instead of stopping.
risks.mitigation: The key masks the item's name, its retry job's name and any job-id-shaped token, then collapses whitespace. A missed match costs at most more items paused, each with a visible note; the budget and job limit still bound the run. The unit test pins the masking for realistic reasons.

risks.risk: Two items rejected for an unrelated reason that reads identically (for example a generic 'verifier rejected') are taken as shared and stop the batch.
risks.mitigation: This matches the stated rule, and the stop names the item and the note names both. The empty-reason case is excluded. The brief's accepted reading is the rule, not a looser one.

risks.risk: Many existing tests rely on the old stop. The Before::RepeatedFailure seeding runs through two workers and timing waits (`wait_for`), and a second failing item changes its ordering.
risks.mitigation: Rework the seeding with `bad` and `bad2`, both failing with a reason; `new` waits for 'end bad2-retry'. Keep the row counts asserted at 6819-6820. Run the file in full before finishing.

risks.risk: Short test item names break substring replacement in the cause key.
risks.mitigation: Whole-token matching only, with a unit test using the names 'a' and 'checks failed'.

risks.risk: A failed item in `report.queued` is retried by the next `athena drain`, which could loop on a permanently failing item across runs.
risks.mitigation: This matches how Paused and Skipped items already behave, and the note says the item was paused for this run. A persistent pause is out of scope (it would touch the scope guard) and was not requested.

risks.risk: The decision-number and docs checks (xtask policy or records tests) may impose a format on docs/decisions.md.
risks.mitigation: Copy the heading and section shape of an adjacent entry such as D153, and run cargo test --locked.

demonstrations.method: Serial stub drain of items a, b where only a fails twice; assert b runs and lands, and the stop is not a repeated failure.
demonstrations.observes: The stub is Stub { items: ["a","b","c"?], outcomes: [Rejected, Rejected, Landed, ...], ratings: ... }. The log reads read a, run a, reread a, run a-retry, read b, run b, land b. report.stop != Stop::RepeatedFailure, report.failed_item is None, and a's job lines are rejected.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the change, finish sets Stop::RepeatedFailure after a's second failure, so the log ends at 'run a-retry', b is never read, and the assertions on 'read b' and on the stop fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point drain::drain(&stub, limits(9.0), &Quiet), which reaches Drain::attempts then Drain::finish. The fake is the existing `Stub` in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (lines 41-296), injected as `&dyn Steps`. Its `outcomes` field scripts a's two rejections, then a landing. The seam exists today and needs no change; the new test is the only addition.

demonstrations.method: Serial stub drain where items a and b each fail twice with the same reason, and a third item c is queued; assert the batch stops naming b and never starts c.
demonstrations.observes: The default Stub rejects every run with reason 'ended rejected', so a and b get one key. The log is read a, run a, reread a, run a-retry, read b, run b, reread b, run b-retry, with no 'read c'. report.stop == Stop::RepeatedFailure and failed_item == Some("b"). A note names item a. display::drain contains 'repeated failure: item b failed twice'. A variant with unlandable a and b ('checks failed') covers the not-landed path.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the shared-cause comparison were missing (a lone failure always passes over), the drain would run c and end QueueEmpty. If the old rule stayed, it would stop at a. Either way the assertions on the stop naming b, or on 'read c' being absent, fail.
